label: first token is e or z; or <DEL> in length-3 sequences
explanation: Two unrelated components. (1) Step 0 when the first original token is e or z: fires on every such step (precision 1.0), at a fixed low magnitude (about 0.16 of max for e, 0.11 for z). This is about 62% of activation mass. (2) The <DEL> step of short sequences, mainly L=3 (about half of L=3 delimiters fire) and more weakly L=4. These are the strongest activations (top examples reach 1.0), and they depend on content: they fire when the prefix holds tokens like l, v, i, h, k, r, 2, 3 and not when it holds e, z, x, d, q. Restricting to those prefix tokens raises dev F1 from 0.85 to 0.87. Small residue: original step 3 on tokens such as e, w, g (about 5% of mass). It never fires in the copy phase, at steps 1-2 or 5 and later, or on repeated tokens.
